info.name: Mesh Connect Integration Managed Transfers API
info.description:
Mesh allows users to connect accounts of financial institutions,
crypto exchanges, and self-custody wallets. Mesh handles credential
validation, MFA, and error handling for each integration. After
an account is connected, Mesh allows client applications to read holdings,
transaction history and balances and execute crypto transfers (with user approval).

request.description:
**Get supported networks list.**

---
Get the list of all networks supported by Mesh to perform transfers, including which tokens and integrations are supported.

The response always includes validation data:
- `addressPattern`: The regex pattern for validating addresses on this network
- `contractAddress`: For each token, the contract address (if applicable) to enable ERC20 contract address validation
- `requiresAddressTag`: Whether a deposit to this network must carry a destination tag/memo (`addressTag`),
e.g. XRP Ledger, Stellar or Cosmos-family networks. Funds sent without the tag may be lost. Just-in-Time (JIT)
address providers must return `addressTag` for these networks, or Mesh rejects the address.

request.description:
**Get the list of networks and tokens eligible for a transfer, based on the provided request data.**

---
The API client provides `FromAuthToken` that represents the source account and the list of target addresses
using the `ToAddresses` field. Front API verifies the addresses and returns the list of tokens eligible
to be transferred as the result of the operation.

Returns the list of holdings on the account that can be used to perform the transfer. Each holdings item
contains the list of supported networks that can be used to transfer the corresponding asset.
Each network contains details such as gas fees and the amount eligible to be transferred.

request.description:
**Validate and preview the transfer.**

---
Validates the transfer, calculates the relevant amount in crypto if requested amount was in fiat and updates
the current network fee values.

This endpoint uses the `NetworkId` field to specify which network will be used to perform the transfer. The target `NetworkId`
should be selected after configuring the transfer using `/configure` endpoint.

Returns the `PreviewId` value that can be used to commit the transfer.

**Commit the previously previewed transfer.**

---

Handles multi-factor authentication codes if the account is configured to use them for additional security.

Returns the status of the transfer and the details of the transfer if it was initiated successfully.

request.description:
Resolves the effective client/sub-client transfer limit before a Link session exists, so an
integrator can filter payment options on their own checkout before opening the widget.
Both bounds are inclusive: an amount is transferable when
`minimumTransferAmountInFiat account-level limits only. The amount a specific route will accept is
`Max(account, network, link-token)` for the floor and `Min(...)` for the cap, so a
particular integration may still reject an amount that falls inside these bounds.
The result depends only on the client and sub-client, so it is safe to cache per sub-client.
